page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server optimized for high-performance computing. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps utilizing the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU physics and extended instruction tests. Large-block memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 695.05 GB/sec for read operations and 347.3 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance is also strong, as evidenced by Geekbench and PassMark CPU encryption scores.

The lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, making this server less suitable for local-storage-heavy databases or GPU-accelerated deep learning. However, the high memory-to-core ratio and 150 Gbps network bandwidth offer excellent qualitative cost efficiency for distributed, memory-intensive compute workloads. It is highly suited for high-performance computing (HPC), large-scale scientific simulations, software compilation, Redis-based in-memory caching, and multi-threaded data processing.
